sections.h2: What the Maricopa County Recorder does
sections.html:
Land records in the county live at the Maricopa County Recorder's Office, which also handles voter registration and mail voting. It reports more than 52 million recorded documents and more than 2.6 million eligible voters. A seller deals with two kinds of paper here: the deed that passes title to the buyer, and the lender's release when the old loan is paid off.

Staff won't advise on legal questions, fill in forms for you or notarize anything. Unsure which form you need? Ask a title company, estate planner or attorney. Call the recording line at 602-506-3535 for process questions.

With 4,420,568 residents in the 2020 census, Maricopa is Arizona's largest county, covering fifteen cities and ten towns. One downtown office takes recordings for all of them, whether the house is in Phoenix, Gila Bend or Wickenburg.

sections.h2: Where and how to record a deed
sections.html:
Three routes exist: walk in, mail it, or submit electronically. Whatever you choose, send an original or a certified copy issued by a government agency. Walk-ins go to Suite 200 at 301 W Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003, weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. except holidays. No appointment is required, and you leave with your original in hand.

  • Counter: pay with cash, card or a check made out to Maricopa County Recorder.
  • Mail: address the envelope to Attn. Copy Desk and enclose a check, cashier's check or money order. Expect the recorded original back at your return address after 2 to 4 weeks. Same-day recording of mailed items isn't promised.
  • Electronic: digital accounts are meant for high-volume filers. If you have one document, a third-party submitter can send it for you.

In practice the title or escrow company files the deed at closing, so you rarely visit. Your part is signing the deed and its affidavit correctly ahead of closing day.

Plan the order of events this way: you sign at the title company, the buyer's funds arrive, and the deed is submitted for recording. If a signature is missing or a name is misspelled, recording stalls and closing can slip, so ask the title officer to review the deed with you a few days early, so there is time to fix it.

A.R.S. 11-475 sets the usual charge at $30 for each document, however many pages it runs. Other charges are below.

Document or serviceRecording fee
Most documents (not plats or surveys)$30
Government agency recording, most documents$15
Plats and surveys, first page$24
Plats and surveys, each added page$20
Copy of a recorded document, per page$1
Certification, per document$3
Military discharge documents$0
Child support documents$0

Fees are collected before recording, so a mailed deed has to arrive with the correct total. Your title company can tell you about other charges that may show on your settlement statement.

sections.h2: What a Maricopa County deed must include
sections.html:
Every deed carries one of two things: an Affidavit of Property Value, or an exemption code written on the deed. The affidavit reports the price and date of the sale plus other deal terms. Staff can't choose an exemption code for you.

A.R.S. 11-1133 governs it. Both parties, or their agents, sign the Department of Revenue form, and it applies to deeds and to contracts of sale. The form collects:

  • Contact details for the buyer and the seller
  • Who should receive the tax statement, and where
  • Legal description, street address and assessor's parcel number
  • Sale date, total consideration, cash down and financing type
  • A yes or no on whether personal property is 5% or more of the price
  • How the parties are related and whether the buyer will live in the house or rent it out

An incomplete affidavit means the recorder must turn the deed away, unless an exemption is noted on it. Layout of the document itself, such as caption and margins, follows A.R.S. 11-480 and the office's form requirements page.

sections.h2: How recording connects to property tax
sections.html:
Once the deed is recorded, the Assessor knows the new owner and the mailing address for the tax statement. The Treasurer bills that person from then on. A fall sale raises one question: was the first half paid? It comes due October 1, and late status starts after 5:00 p.m. on November 1, which in 2026 shifted to November 2 because the first was a Sunday. Pay the whole year by December 31 and no interest applies.

The tax also works as a lien. A.R.S. 42-17153 has it taking hold each January 1, ahead of most other claims on the house. Expect the title company to pay anything unpaid out of your sale proceeds. Call the Maricopa County Treasurer at 602-506-8511 for what is owed.

A free alert service called Maricopa Title Alert, run through the Recorder's Office and linked from the Assessor's site, notifies you when a document is registered against your property. Heirs and out-of-state owners find it handy. One bill from the Treasurer spans more than 1,800 tax districts: cities, schools, community colleges and special districts. Money left over after a foreclosure sale is posted on the Treasurer's site under A.R.S. 33-812.

Run through these before anything goes to the counter.

  • Spelling of every name, including a trust, matches how title is held.
  • Legal description and parcel number copy the previous deed.
  • The affidavit is signed, or the exemption code appears on the deed.
  • You have a signed original with the notary section filled in.
  • Your return address sits at the upper left of page one.
  • The check covers $30 for every document in the stack.

Houses that pass through probate or a trust often need several deeds, and each one is charged separately. Have the title company list every document and give you one total.

A cash sale follows the same path: one deed, one affidavit, one fee. What it skips is the buyer's lender, so there is usually no new deed of trust to record. Your own old loan still ends with a release, though. After closing, ask the title company to confirm that release was recorded, and file the recorded copy with your sale papers.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost in Maricopa County?
faqs.a: The usual price is $30 a document, whatever the page count. Plats and surveys run $24 for page one and $20 for each page after. Copies cost $1 a page and certifying a document costs $3.

faqs.q: Where do I take a deed to be recorded in Maricopa County?
faqs.a: Go to the downtown office, Suite 200 at 301 W Jefferson St in Phoenix. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, holidays excluded, and walk-ins need no appointment.

faqs.q: Is it okay to mail my deed to the Maricopa County Recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the original to Attn. Copy Desk at the downtown address with a check, cashier's check or money order. It comes back to your return address within 2 to 4 weeks, and the office doesn't commit to recording on the day it arrives.

faqs.q: Do I need an Affidavit of Property Value to record a Maricopa County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the deed shows an exemption code. A.R.S. 11-1133 sets the requirement, and the recorder has to refuse a deed that has neither a complete affidavit nor an exemption notation.

faqs.q: Can the Maricopa County Recorder's staff help me prepare a deed?
faqs.a: No. They don't give legal advice, help with forms or notarize. A title company, estate planner or attorney can prepare it, and 602-506-3535 reaches the recording line for process questions.
